A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the inverse gap equations provide a very good description of the low-energy states in the odd tin isotopes and, with the help of a number-projected treatment, also in the even tin isotopes, if a Gaussian two-body interaction is applied.
the number-projected FBCS model with the inverse gap equations and the two-Gaussian forces is able to reproduce a large number of spectroscopic quantities in a consistent way.
the number-projected FBCS model with two Gaussian interactions reproduces the experimental data on the tin isotopes quite well.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FBCS model with the number-projected diagonalization is able to reproduce the experimental data with the same interaction parameters as the BCS model.
the FBCS model, with its simple structure, is a very useful tool to describe nuclear ground-state properties.
the number-projected BCS treatment is a viable alternative to the usual BCS approach for the even tin isotopes.
